newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Brazil shares end lower despite Wall Street's rise.
newsitem.headline: Brazil shares end lower despite Wall Street's rise.

text.p: Brazil shares ended 1.12 percent lower on Tuesday, breaking stride with U.S. stocks, which jumped again after the U.S. Federal Reserve decided to leave U.S. rates unchanged, brokers said.
The Bovespa index .BVSP of the 47 most traded stocks ended at 11,211 points. Total market turnover was lighter-than-average at 773.1 million reais ($715.8 million).
"The local bolsa recently has been tracking Wall Street, but today the market moved in an opposite direction," a senior trader said.

Analysts said the decline in Brazil partly reflected a decision by the Superior Justice Tribunal to postpone a decision on a long-running dispute over a Telebras share issue. A ruling could have an impact on the stock price.
Telebras preferred dropped 2.16 percent to close at 136 reais.

Among other leading blue-chips, state oil company Petrobras preferred fell 1.36 percent to 290 reais. Federal power holding company Eletrobras preferred dropped 0.38 percent to 528 reais. Privatized miner CVRD preferred gained 2.27 percent to end at 26.60 reais.
The Sao Paulo bolsa's power sector index .IEE fell 0.91 percent to 3,242 points.
